_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
A path whose every changed file differs from the reviewed state only in
comments and layout has not drifted and needs no entry here. Java,
TypeScript, JavaScript and .properties are read by
frontend/scripts/lib/comment-only.mjs; everything else is compared byte for
byte. The recorded id does not move with such a change, so the next real
change is diffed against the state that was reviewed.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: #997: HandshakeService alone moved under core/init. The app_started audit event's dbSchemaChecksum, the newest applied migration's checksum, becomes dbSchemaChecksums, the version and recorded checksum of every applied migration (V1:<n>,V2:<none>), still non-secret integers from flyway_schema_history, the property 1.1 recorded for the field. Every changed line was read. No key material, KDF, salt, AAD, DPAPI call, crypto.bin handling or storage guard is touched; the API key generation and session.json are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

Unused lambda parameters renamed to `_` (Java unnamed variables) so Eclipse JDT stops flagging them, and nothing else: every changed line was read, each swaps one parameter name for `_` in a lambda whose body never named it. Arity and parameter types are unchanged, so the same overloads resolve and the same code runs. Here: 28 parameters in 15 files of feature/mail/service, mostly TransactionStatus (status), folder executor callbacks (folder, uidFolder, store, resyncEvents), map keys in computeIfAbsent and compute, one RetryContext and one SSE emitter's error; the formatter reflowed one line in MailSyncService. No lock, transaction boundary, folder mode or IMAP command changed. Verdict unchanged.

#928, the trust path, written by the session that records it and waiting for its pass (IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT 1.92, section 1). Every IMAP and SMTP connection now takes its sockets from one shared MailTlsContext instead of the JDK's default SSLContext: anchors are what the default trust manager accepts (TrustManagerFactory.init(null), getAcceptedIssuers), so the trusted roots are unchanged and javax.net.ssl.trustStore is honoured; the Let's Encrypt intermediates and Generation Y cross-signs under backend/src/main/resources/tls (new in Code paths) are a Collection CertStore, path material only, never anchors; revocation stays off as in the JSSE default; mail.<protocol>.socketFactory.fallback=false so a refusal is not retried through the default factory. checkserveridentity, required STARTTLS and the OAuth2 plaintext guards are unchanged. LeafOnlyChainIT fails in five of eight cases with the factory property taken out and in the host-check case with only the fallback property taken out (run and seen). No new egress. Verdict unchanged.

#988: which header tokens count as addresses is EmailAddresses, the rule the compose form validates by, instead of InternetAddress.validate(). HeaderAddresses.parseValidTokens and parseLabel use it, and the STRICT branch of MimeMessageBuilder parses through the new HeaderAddresses.parseAllValid (parseHeader, then the rule for every token) instead of InternetAddress.parse; MailDraftService.extractEmails reads the reply-all fields through parseValidTokens, so one malformed address no longer costs the field. Every changed line was read. A send still fails rather than drop a recipient. B1-5 is not weakened: recipientsDiffer reads the server copy through getRecipients() and keeps an address the rule refuses as its raw lower-cased form, so a recipient the server adds is still a difference; the stored side is filtered by the same rule the draft save writes with, as before with validate(). EmailAddressesTest checks that every accepted vector is one InternetAddress.parse and validate() take whole. The parenthesis in the B1-5 section saying a send parses with InternetAddress.parse is stale and goes at the next re-verification. Verdict unchanged.

MailDraftService.buildQuotedBody writes the quoted original's header from the message bundles in the request's locale (mail.quote.*) instead of Czech literals, formats receivedAt with a localized medium date and short time instead of LocalDateTime.toString, and falls back to mail.message.unknownSender / noSubject where it printed null. MailDraftService gains a MessageSource constructor argument and nothing else changes: every changed line was read. The header is text in the prefilled body the user edits before sending, the same plain text as before; subject, In-Reply-To, References and the reply-all recipients are built exactly as they were, no IMAP or SMTP command, header or bound moves, and the sender and subject it quotes are the stored values the old header printed. The dash frame the attachment reminder stops at is unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

Review follow-up to #1016, in MailDraftService.buildQuotedBody alone: the quoted header's date replaces every horizontal space the formatter writes with a plain space (CLDR's narrow no-break space before AM), and it is formatted in the language of the bundle that answered (its app.locale key) rather than the request's, so a request with no bundle for its language gets the default bundle's labels with a date to match. Every changed line was read. Only text in the prefilled body moves; no IMAP or SMTP command, header, recipient or bound changes. Verdict unchanged.

One argument in OAuth2TokenService#getAccessToken: the missing-refresh-token MAIL_ACCOUNT_REQUIRES_REAUTH now passes the method's own email parameter as {0} of error.mail.accountRequiresReauth, so the user sees which account to sign in again. The address goes to the local client in detail and messageArgs, as error.account.alreadyExists already does; the fallback message the log gets is unchanged and carries no address. The early return before any provider call, the refresh lock, the permanent/transient split and who sets and clears requires_reauth are untouched. Verdict unchanged.

Unused lambda parameters renamed to `_` (Java unnamed variables) so Eclipse JDT stops flagging them, and nothing else: every changed line was read, each swaps one parameter name for `_` in a lambda whose body never named it. Arity and parameter types are unchanged, so the same overloads resolve and the same code runs. Here: the computeIfAbsent key in OAuth2TokenService's per-account refresh lock (id); the lock itself and everything it guards are untouched. Verdict unchanged.

#1028: auth-failed.html only, its words: both language halves explain the failure without "OAuth2 flow" and "authorization code" and no longer send a re-sign-in to Add account, and the reason now shows under a label in each language, in #reason and a new #reason-en. Every changed line was read. The script still writes the ?reason= value with textContent only, so the Failure hygiene claim holds; auth-finished.html is unchanged.

#1029: OAuth2CallbackController#success and auth-failed.html, which move one claim, so the audit says so in 1.10 (§1, failure hygiene) rather than here alone. Every changed line was read. /success now catches what the guards, the persistence and its own two checks throw and redirects to auth-failed.html with a code from a fixed map keyed by message key, login_failed otherwise; no exception text, address or message sentence reaches the URL, and the code is [a-z_] so it needs no encoding. The session invalidation and the authorized-client removal stay in their finally blocks, before and after the catch alike, and the tests assert both on the rejection paths. The page compares the code with the data-reason values of fixed blocks and writes it with textContent; it is never markup or a selector. Logging keeps GlobalExceptionHandler's levels (AppException WARN with the log message, which masks the address at the source; anything else ERROR with the stack). No route, permission, token handling or state check moves. Verdict unchanged.

#1002, a dependabot bump of the github-actions-minor-patch group. The one change in windows-signed-release.yml is the Setup Java step's actions/setup-java, v6.2.0 (77dd5b2c) to v6.3.0 (d1374f8a), still pinned to a 40-hex commit. That step runs in build-signed-windows, the job with contents: read and no updater key; publish-release, which holds the key, does not use setup-java, and none of its lines moved. Every other step, permission, environment, pin and run: block is byte-identical (U-1, U-2 and U-3 hold). v6.3.0 stops registering the Java problem matcher by default, so compiler output no longer becomes pull request annotations; it still fails the build, and nothing here reads those annotations. It also validates the architecture of a JDK file install and adds Microsoft OpenJDK and JetBrains Runtime fixes; the step installs Temurin 25 as before. Verdict unchanged.

The Contact us page. The one change in AboutSettings.svelte is a link to settings/feedback under the diagnostics button, plus the resolve import it needs. The update channel select, the startup-check toggle, checkForUpdateManually and its status line are byte-identical; nothing reaches the updater, its endpoints or its key. Verdict unchanged.

#1021: the one change under frontend/src-tauri/src is in lib.rs, where the main window's builder takes the title "VoxRox Mail" instead of a Czech loading title, with the comment above it rewritten. Every changed line was read. The window label, URL, size, data directory, browser arguments and every other builder call are byte-identical, as are the updater commands (check_for_update, download_pending_update, install_pending_update), the pending-update state, the endpoints, the public key and the capabilities. A window title reaches nothing on the update path. Verdict unchanged.

#1023: BootErrorView.svelte takes errorDetail in place of errorLang. The message under the heading is now always in the interface language (bootFailureText.ts), and the error's own English text moves into a bits-ui Collapsible after the diagnostic actions, closed by default and marked lang=en when shown. Every changed line was read. The manual update check (handleCheckForUpdates, checkForUpdateManually, the aria-disabled button and its status region), the retry and restart handlers and the diagnostic actions are byte-identical; the prompt and failure dialogs stay mounted outside the boot-gated block. Display only; nothing reaches the updater, its endpoints or its key. Verdict unchanged.

#1025: UpdateFailureDialog.svelte keeps update.failure.description alone in the DialogDescription and moves the updater's own message, with its lang, into a bits-ui Collapsible after the button row, closed by default; the releases link keeps RELEASES_URL, target and rel under a new label (update.failure.openReleases, "Otevřít stránku ke stažení"). BootErrorView.svelte only takes its disclosure label from common.technicalDetails instead of app.bootFailure.technicalDetails. Every changed line was read. updateFailureState, showUpdateFailure and dismissUpdateFailure are untouched (updates.ts changed in a comment only), and the dialog still opens with focus on its first control, now pinned on the releases link by the boot e2e test.
